Strategies for improving maintenance of physical activity
While the best diet for long-term obesity treatment is still to be identiﬁed, research consistently indicates that moderate-to-vigorous
PA is integral to long-term weight loss maintenance success. Research in this area primarily focuses on maintaining increases in
moderate-to-vigorous intensity PA.
For individuals with obesity, maintenance of increased PA levels is complicated by physiological, psychological, and envi-
ronmental factors. The main perceived barriers to PA adherence include low ﬁtness, pain, lack of stimuli, body image dissat-
isfaction, time, and weather constraints (Patel et al., 2013). Behavioral and cognitive strategies may mitigate these challenges
to PA adherence (Patel et al., 2013; Dalle Grave et al., 2011). One beneﬁcial technique may be intermittent bouts of exercise,
such as 4 short (10 min) bouts of exercise for at least 5 days a week, vs. one long bout of continuous exercise (Jakicic et al.,
1995). Though one RCT showed promise using this strategy, larger studies were unable to produce comparable outcomes in
